card.name: Ghumura
card.tagline: Kalahandi's heroic pot-drum war dance of Odisha
card.profile: Ghumura (Ghumra) is a folk dance of the Kalahandi district of western Odisha, named after the ghumura - a pitcher-shaped earthen kettle-drum tied to the dancer's neck whose face is traditionally covered with monitor-lizard skin (Wikipedia; Swadesi). Classed as folk though its mudras carry classical resemblance, it began as a 'Veera Vadya' war dance used to embolden soldiers and is now performed during Nuakhai and Dussehra. It is male-oriented, performed in lines or geometric formations by 15-40 dancers, accompanied by nishan, dhol, taal and madal, and linked in myth to the Chandi Purana account of Durga's battle against Mahishasura (Wikipedia; IJHSSI).
card.insight: Ghumura has represented India at international events; about 100 dancers from Bhawanipatna performed it at the Republic Day Parade in New Delhi on 26 January 1999, and troupes performed at the Bharat Utsav in Moscow in July 2025 (Grokipedia, citing event records).
